items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to gratuities received
by third-party food delivery workers
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4927

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to gratuities
received by third-party food delivery workers

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to mandate that all third-party food deliv-
ery services include the option to include gratuity payments while the
delivery order is placed

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 Adds new section 391-W of the general business law, which
establishes that third-party food delivery services shall provide an
option to include gratuity payments at the same point of the ordering
process when the underlying order is placed, and sets terms for penal-
ties for violations of this section and enforcement thereof.

Section 2 Sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Third-party food delivery services have made gratuity payment more
difficult in response to recent New York City minimum wage reforms.
While it is illegal for third-party food delivery services to block
payment of gratuities to workers, some have altered their platforms'
gratuity payment procedures so as to occur after the order has been
assigned to a delivery worker. This drastically undercuts both the total
amount of gratuities paid and the workers' agency in choosing the most
lucrative recent orders in the local area.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2023-24: S9482 (Ramos) Referred to Consumer Protection / A10595
(Mitaynes)

 
FISCAL IMPACT:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effective immediately

B.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to the payment of
gratuities for orders placed through third-party food delivery services and
third-party grocery delivery services
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4927B

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to the payment of
gratuities for orders placed through third-party food delivery services
and third-party grocery delivery services

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to mandate that all third-party food deliv-
ery services include the option to include gratuity payments while the
delivery order is placed.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds new section 391-vv of the general business law, which
establishes that third-party food delivery services and third-party
grocery delivery services shall provide an option to include gratuity
payments at the same point of the ordering process when the underlying
order is placed, defines applicable delivery services and workers, and
sets terms for penalties for violations of this section and enforcement
thereof.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

The B print includes third-party grocery delivery services and workers.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Third-party food delivery services have made gratuity payment more
difficult in response to recent New York City minimum wage refoinis.
While it is illegal for third-party food delivery services to block
payment of gratuities to workers, some have altered their platforms'
gratuity payment procedures so as to occur after the order has been
assigned to a delivery worker. This drastically undercuts both the total
amount of gratuities paid and the workers' agency in choosing the most
lucrative recent orders in the local area.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2023-24: S9482 (Ramos) Referred to Consumer Protection / A10595
(Mitaynes)  
FISCAL IMPACT:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately

summary: Requires third-party food delivery services and third-party grocery delivery services to provide the ability to include a gratuity at the same point in the online order process when the underlying order is placed; provides that customers shall not be required to pay a gratuity; provides that third-party food delivery services and third-party grocery delivery services shall not reduce the compensation of any worker as a result of gratuities; establishes penalties for violations of such provisions.
